maelstrom

MAYL-strum · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Maelstrom is a state of wild, chaotic disorder.

Backstage during intermission was a maelstrom of costume changes, missed cues, and whispered arguments.

Example

When the fire alarm went off during the assembly, the gym became a maelstrom of shoving, dropped backpacks, and shouted directions from every side.

Maelstrom describes an overwhelming, chaotic swirl of activity -- more than ordinary busyness, closer to pandemonium.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

frenzy: A frenzy is a burst of wild, racing activity or emotion in people -- shoppers in a frenzy, a frenzy of last-minute studying. A maelstrom is the scene itself: a churning swirl of disorder that swallows everything in it. Frenzy names the energy; maelstrom names the chaos around it.

whirlwind: A whirlwind is a rush of activity that moves almost too fast to follow, yet a whirlwind can be perfectly organized -- a wedding day timed to the minute is a whirlwind. A maelstrom is never organized: it is wild, churning disorder with no one in charge.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

calm: a peaceful, undisturbed state

tranquility: a state of quiet, untroubled peace

Where it sits · how far out of control things are — commotion → maelstrom → pandemonium

commotion vs. maelstrom: A commotion is far milder than a maelstrom: a dropped tray can cause a commotion, a brief burst of noise and disturbance, while a maelstrom pulls a whole scene into churning disorder.

pandemonium vs. maelstrom: Pandemonium is even wilder than a maelstrom: a maelstrom is overwhelming, swirling disorder, but pandemonium means every last shred of control is gone from the room.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — mael-

root — mael-: to grind, whirl (Middle Dutch malen)

root — -strom

root — -strom: stream, current (Middle Dutch stroom, cognate with English "stream")

Put it together

Put it together: Maelstrom combines mael- ("to grind or whirl") with strom ("stream, current") -- it was originally the name of a real, ferocious whirlpool off the coast of Norway, and the word later came to describe any scene of violent, swirling chaos.

Use the root in a new word: stream

Use the root in a new word: stream: A narrow stream cut through the forest, growing wider with every mile toward the sea.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Maelstrom is a strong, almost literary word for chaos -- originally a real whirlpool -- so save it for genuinely overwhelming disorder, not everyday busyness.
